claims.text: The UT San Antonio prototype carries four optical water-level sensors set at different heights.
claims.quote: four optical water-level sensors mounted at varying heights
claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.text: The prototype also senses temperature, humidity, light and precipitation.
claims.quote: The resulting prototype combines temperature, humidity, light and precipitation sensing
claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.text: The release describes a field-ready prototype that pairs solar energy harvesting with several sensors, long-range radios and machine learning on the device.
claims.quote: the team engineered a field-ready prototype that combines solar energy harvesting, multi-sensor environmental tracking, long-range wireless radios and on-device machine learning
claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.text: The node runs TinyML, which the release defines as a branch of computer science that shrinks machine learning algorithms to run on small low-power microcontrollers.
claims.quote: using TinyML — a branch of computer science that compresses machine learning algorithms so they can run directly on small, low-power microcontrollers
claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.text: The model on the device judges imminent local flood risk from current and recent sensor readings with no central server involved.
claims.quote: This on-device AI evaluates current and recent sensor data to predict localized, imminent flood risk without relying on a central server.
claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.text: Chen Pan calls the system an off-grid design that makes its own power and judges flood risk on the device itself.
claims.quote: Our system is an off-grid solution. It generates its own power, evaluates flood risk locally right on the device and sends timely warnings without needing external electricity or expensive network lines.
claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.text: The release reports that the model reached 98.82% validation accuracy in initial assessments after training.
claims.quote: achieving 98.82% validation accuracy in initial assessments post-training
claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.text: The node runs on its own solar power system, which charges a built-in battery and backup energy storage.
claims.quote: the sensing node relies on a self-sustaining solar power system. An onboard power chip collects ambient light to charge a built-in battery and backup energy storage units
claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.text: The node sends LoRa radio signals that the release says reach more than a half-mile through city streets and up to five miles in open areas.
claims.quote: it sends lightweight radio signals using LoRa (Long Range) wireless technology. These low-power signals can travel more than a half-mile through city streets and up to five miles in open areas
claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.text: Data from many nodes goes to a central monitoring site, where a second and larger AI model builds an interactive web dashboard with predictive maps.
claims.quote: At the central monitoring site, custom server software aggregates data from multiple deployed nodes across a town or watershed. A second, larger AI model analyzes spatial and temporal patterns across the network to generate an interactive web dashboard with predictive maps.
claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.text: Parts for one prototype sensing station cost roughly $150 to $220, according to the release.
claims.quote: The total cost of parts for one prototype sensing station ranges from roughly $150 to $220.
claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.text: Chen Pan is seeking a patent on the hardware architecture. The team aims to refine the prototype into a weatherized commercial product.
claims.quote: Pan is currently pursuing patent protection for the hardware architecture. The team aims to refine the design into a sleeker, weatherized commercial product
claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.text: Chen Pan, an assistant professor of electrical engineering in the UT San Antonio Klesse College of Engineering and Integrated Design, leads the work.
claims.quote: Led by Chen Pan , PhD, assistant professor of electrical engineering in the Margie and Bill Klesse College of Engineering and Integrated Design
claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.text: The team includes Mimi Xie of UT San Antonio along with Hua Zhang and Wenlu Wang of Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi.
claims.quote: The team includes Mimi Xie , assistant professor of computer science in the UT San Antonio College of AI, Cyber and Computing, as well as Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi collaborators Hua Zhang , professor of engineering, and Wenlu Wang , assistant professor of computer science.
claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.quote: From coastal bends facing storm surges to low-water crossings in San Antonio, flood risks often spike block by block long before regional alerts sound.
claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods

claims.quote: While regional weather models and satellite imaging offer essential big-picture forecasts, they can miss hyper-local flash floods.
claims.document: UT San Antonio Today, UT San Antonio researcher builds self-powered, smart warning system to catch local floods
